findings.unwaivableWhy: Nobody may wave this through on their own: it touches money. A charge, a price or a refund that goes out wrong costs a real person real money.

gaps.what: None of this project's own tests were run, because there are none this tool can find.
gaps.why: This project has no test script, so there is no suite to harvest journeys from. A test suite is the only source that walks this product with the arguments somebody actually thought about, so without one the check compares what it can read and call for itself, and no more.
gaps.unlockedBy: Point the project at vitest or Node's own test runner and every test file becomes a journey, run twice on each build and compared.

gaps.what: Anything the old build never had a record for.
gaps.why: The old build was only booted to re-check the differences already suspected, not to walk everything.
gaps.unlockedBy: Run with --paired to boot the old build and walk every journey against it.

gaps.what: "ask greet to print its help, and compare every word of it": quick. That is recorded and NOT compared: a stopwatch on a shared machine measures the machine as much as the product, so a busy laptop would otherwise invent a slowdown that nobody caused. A build that hangs is still caught — it gets stopped for taking too long, and how it finished is compared.
gaps.why: a stopwatch measures how busy this machine was at least as much as it measures the product, so the number is recorded and never compared (measures the machine)
gaps.unlockedBy: Nothing. This is deliberate and permanent — the effect is watched at the call, never at the result.

gaps.what: Files written into .git, .staysfixed, node_modules were not watched. node_modules is the one that costs something: a build step that patches a dependency, generates a client into it, or rebuilds a native module changes what ships and is not seen here. It is left out because fingerprinting it twice per run makes a check nobody waits for. Name it under "process.alsoWatch" in the settings to watch it anyway.
gaps.why: the value was too large to keep, so only a fingerprint of it was kept (too big)
gaps.unlockedBy: Nothing. This is deliberate and permanent — the effect is watched at the call, never at the result.

gaps.unlockedBy: 3 of them could be covered by journeys that reach them — read out of your source, or named by hand in a journeys file.

gaps.what: This coverage count is less exact than it looks.
gaps.why: No journey here has steps that name the door they knock on, so a door counts as opened only when something was observed at its own address. A route and a command are both addressed to the journey rather than to the door, so those 2 are undercounted. Walk the journeys the code reader generates and the answer becomes exact.
gaps.unlockedBy: Read the caveat: it says what would make it exact.

gaps.what: This coverage count is less exact than it looks.
gaps.why: Nothing here knows which functions the test suite ran, so an exported name counts as opened only if a journey addressed it directly — which is why 1 of them read as never opened. Install the test runner's coverage package and the suite says exactly what it touched.
gaps.unlockedBy: Read the caveat: it says what would make it exact.

summary: 1 thing behaves differently, checked against 1.0.0, run live. Running the new build twice showed 0 addresses that will not sit still, and 12 that do. 0 differences landed on the unsteady ones and were dropped; 1 remains. Nothing that used to be steady has become unpredictable. Everything reported here was re-checked against the old build booted live, so none of it is drift. What is NOT reported rests on the stored record from the last time the old build ran — a difference the store never captured cannot show up in this list. NOT EVERYTHING WAS CHECKED: 3 of the 3 ways into this product have never been walked through, so nothing here says anything about them, and 5 other things were not looked at (None of this project's own tests were run, because there are none this tool can find, and more). A clean result only covers what was walked — `staysfixed coverage` has the whole list.
